message.content:
Driving from **San Francisco** to **Los Angeles** covers roughly **380–400 miles** (≈610‑640 km), depending on your exact route.  

Under ideal freeway conditions—steady flow on I‑80 E into I‑580 E then I‑680 S/CA‑99 S toward I‑5 N—the trip takes about **5½ to 6 hours** if you maintain an average speed around 60–70 mph (95–110 kph).

In practice:

| Factor | Typical impact |
|--------|----------------|
| Morning or evening rush hour near Bay Area exits / CA‑101 & I‑5 entry points | +30 min – 1 hr |
| Weather (fog, rain, snow) | +15 min – 45 min |
| Construction or detours | +10 min – 30 min per incident |
| Traffic incidents (accidents, road closures) | Variable |

So expect somewhere between **5½ and 7 hours**, with most trips falling close to the lower end during light traffic days. If you’re planning a specific departure time, checking real‑time navigation apps like Google Maps or Waze just before you leave gives the best current estimate.
